Lonial found an issue that despite user- and BPF-side frozen BPF map
(like in case of .rodata)
column2: it was still possible to write into it from

column1: a BPF program side through specific helpers having ARG_PTR_TO_{LONG
as arguments.
In check_func_arg() when the argument is as mentioned
is never set. Later
PTR_TO_MAP_VALUE as register base type
subsequent call to check_map_access_type() and given the BPF map is
read-only it succeeds.
The helpers really need to be annotated as ARG_PTR_TO_{LONG
when results are written into them as opposed to read out of them. The
latter indicates that it's okay to pass a pointer to uninitialized memory
as the memory is written to anyway.
However
column3: INT} is a special case of ARG_PTR_TO_FIXED_SIZE_MEM

column1: just with additional alignment requirement. So it is better to just get
rid of the ARG_PTR_TO_{LONG
column2: INT} special cases altogether and reuse the

column1: fixed size memory types. For this
alignment given these helpers write directly into the args via *<ptr> = val.
The .arg*_size has been initialized reflecting the actual sizeof(*<ptr>).
MEM_ALIGNED can only be used in combination with MEM_FIXED_SIZE annotated
argument types
column2: since in !MEM_FIXED_SIZE cases the verifier does not know

column1: the buffer size a priori and therefore cannot blindly write *<ptr> = val.
